title: Why 40% of Men Won't Admit They're Struggling (And What It's Costing Them)
description:
Break your arm and people sign your cast. Tell someone you haven't slept in three weeks because your chest feels like it's caving in — and the room goes quiet. That double standard is not random. It is the result of a definition of strength that was wrong from the start, and nobody told us.

I spent years white-knuckling life — passive-aggressive in meetings, snapping at people I cared about, awake at 3am running mental loops I couldn't switch off. I told myself that was the cost of ambition. It wasn't. It was a person who needed help and had no framework for asking for it.

In this video I go through why the stigma exists and where it comes from, what the research actually says about men and mental health (the numbers are not abstract), a story about sitting in my car after work unable to go upstairs, the moment I realized listening beats solving, why the personal trainer analogy changes how you think about therapy, and what breaking stigma actually looks like at the level most of us operate at.
